stories.headline: PCE HITS 3.8%, HIGHEST SINCE MAY 2023, AS IRAN WAR DRIVES GASOLINE UP 5.5%
stories.body: April PCE rose 0.4% month-over-month, pushing the 12-month rate from 3.5% to 3.8% — the hottest reading in nearly three years. Goods prices jumped 0.7%, led by a 5.5% gasoline surge tied to Strait of Hormuz disruptions. Core PCE held at 3.3% YoY, suggesting energy shock hasn't yet embedded into services inflation, but the Fed remains frozen: FedWatch prices a 98.8% probability of a hold at the June meeting.

stories.headline: SNOWFLAKE SURGES 36% ON $6B AWS AI DEAL, DRAGGING S&P 500 AND NASDAQ TO RECORD CLOSES
stories.body: Snowflake (SNOW) posted its best day ever after reporting Q1 FY27 revenue of $1.39B (+33% YoY) and a landmark $6B multi-year collaboration with AWS. The AI data platform rally lifted the broader software sector: ServiceNow and Oracle each gained 6%, Palantir jumped 8%, and Microsoft added 3%+. The S&P 500 closed at a record 7,564 (+0.58%) and Nasdaq hit 26,917 (+0.91%), defying the 3.8% PCE print.

stories.headline: U.S. STRIKES IRAN MILITARY SITES AS HORMUZ CEASEFIRE DEAL REACHES DRAFT STAGE
stories.body: The U.S. carried out new airstrikes in southern Iran targeting sites threatening Strait of Hormuz maritime traffic, while U.S. and Iranian negotiators simultaneously finalized a draft framework to extend the ceasefire and gradually reopen the strait. Trump and Khamenei have not yet given final approval. WTI bounced to ~$90 on the strike news after falling 10%+ since May 18 on deal optimism.

stories.headline: MICHIGAN WINS 2026 NCAA TITLE; PROGRAMS REBUILD ROSTERS THROUGH TRANSFER PORTAL
stories.body: The Michigan Wolverines claimed their second national championship on April 6, capping the 2026 season. With the portal now mostly closed (3,662 players entered; 76% committed), programs are finalizing lineups for 2026-27. Washington has filled 12 of 15 roster spots, including commitments from 3-star SF Lattimore Ford and Brazilian pro Wini Braga.

stories.headline: OKC LEADS SPURS 3-2, GAME 6 TONIGHT; KNICKS SWEEP CAVS TO REACH FIRST FINALS SINCE 1999
stories.body: The Western Conference Finals continue tonight at 8:30 PM ET on NBC/Peacock as OKC hosts San Antonio in a potential closeout Game 6 (Spurs can force Game 7 on Saturday). In the East, the New York Knicks swept the Cleveland Cavaliers to clinch their first NBA Finals appearance since 1999. The Finals begin June 3.

stories.headline: PACKERS RB JOSH JACOBS ARRESTED ON DOMESTIC ABUSE CHARGES DURING OTA WEEK
stories.body: Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs was arrested Tuesday on five charges including domestic abuse battery, strangulation/suffocation, and intimidation of a victim. The Packers head coach deferred to the team's statement and said they will 'let the process play out.' Elsewhere, Raiders TE Brock Bowers declared himself 100% healthy after a knee injury limited him to 12 games in 2025.

stories.headline: TEXAS TECH QB SORSBY ENTERS TREATMENT FOR GAMBLING ADDICTION; TRANSFER PORTAL CLOSES
stories.body: Texas Tech QB Brendan Sorsby — rated the No. 2 overall prospect in the 2026 transfer portal — took an indefinite leave to enter a residential treatment facility for a gambling addiction. In other portal news, Sam Leavitt (Arizona State QB who helped lead the team to the CFP) committed to LSU, joining OT Jordan Seaton (Colorado → LSU) in Lane Kiffin's major portal haul.

deepDive.title: How the Strait of Hormuz Keeps the Fed Frozen
content: Today's PCE print — 3.8% year-over-year, the highest since May 2023 — landed with an important qualifier: the inflation wasn't broad-based. Gasoline surged 5.5% in April alone, driving goods prices up 0.7% while core PCE (excluding food and energy) came in at a still-elevated 3.3%. The engine behind that gasoline spike is a geography problem. Since late February, Iran has effectively blocked the Strait of Hormuz — the 33-mile-wide chokepoint through which roughly 20% of the world's seaborne oil supply flows. Until that changes, the Fed's rate path is essentially held hostage to a geopolitical negotiation.

Here's how oil reaches your PCE basket. Gasoline accounts for roughly 3.5% of the headline PCE weight. A 5.5% monthly surge in that sub-index adds approximately 0.19 percentage points to the monthly headline PCE reading — nearly half of the total 0.4% monthly gain. Beyond direct energy, oil flows into the cost of transporting goods, heating commercial space, and manufacturing inputs, creating secondary pressure across the basket. PCE's chain-weighting continuously adjusts for consumer substitution (shifting to cheaper fuel grades, carpooling), but it can't avoid the shock when all energy grades spike simultaneously, as they did in April.

The Federal Reserve's clearest precedent is the 1973-74 oil embargo. When OPEC cut exports, the Fed initially held back, treating energy inflation as a supply-side problem outside its mandate. Headline CPI surged past 12%, wages followed, and the Fed was forced into a brutal tightening cycle regardless. In 2022, facing Ukraine-driven energy inflation, the Fed moved early and aggressively to break the cycle before second-round wage effects set in — and it worked. Today, core PCE at 3.3% remains well above the 2% target, and CME FedWatch now prices just a 0.6% probability of any rate cut at the June meeting.

What makes the Hormuz situation analytically interesting is how directly a peace deal would show up in the numbers. If Trump and Khamenei approve the current draft ceasefire — which reportedly includes phased Strait reopening — WTI would likely fall toward $72-75 based on pre-crisis supply-demand models. At that price, the gasoline PCE sub-index would reverse 3-4 months of gains. Within two monthly PCE readings, headline inflation could mechanically drop 0.4-0.5 percentage points, bringing the annual rate closer to 3.3-3.4%. That's the single most powerful catalyst for a 2026 rate cut: not a GDP print, not a jobs number, but a ceasefire agreement. Watch the diplomacy as closely as the economic calendar.
